deriver.isa-armv8-sha.label: AArch64 · ARMv8 SHA2 extension
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.registers.label: AArch64 · ARMv8 SHA2 · vector registers
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.sha256h: Four rounds, first half: the destination holds A, B, C, D (A in the lowest word) and receives A … D after the fourth round; the second operand holds E … H, the third K+W of the four rounds.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.sha256h2: Four rounds, second half: the destination holds E, F, G, H and receives E … H after the fourth round. It needs A … D from before these rounds, which sha256h has just overwritten, so it reads the copy.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.copyAbcd: sha256h and sha256h2 work as a pair: sha256h overwrites A … D, but sha256h2 for the same rounds still needs the old A … D. That is why the compiler copies A … D first; sha256h works on the copy.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.copyEfgh: A copy of E … H for sha256h2 to overwrite: the original stays untouched for the feed-forward at the end of the block.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.literalK: Loads K{{first}}…K{{last}} from the literal pool next to the code (adrp gives the page, ldr the offset), often well before the rounds that use them.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.scheduleAhead: The message schedule runs ahead: this instruction works on W{{first}}…W{{last}} several rounds before the state view's schedule steps write them. The four message registers hold a sliding window of 16 schedule words.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.sha512.label: AArch64 · ARMv8.2 SHA512 extension
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.sha512h: Two rounds, first half: the destination holds h + K + W of both rounds (round t in the upper half) and receives T1 of both rounds; the second operand holds (f, g), the third (d, e) from before the rounds.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.sha512h2: Two rounds, second half: the destination holds the two T1 values and receives the new (a, b); the second operand holds (c, d), the third (a, b) from before the rounds.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.newE: The new (e, f) of both rounds: d + T1, lane by lane. The old (a, b) is now (c, d) and the old (e, f) is now (g, h), so five registers rotate through the state without any copy.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.addKw512: Adds the round constants to the schedule words: K + W of two rounds.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.addHkw: Adds h to K + W: h + K + W is the input sha512h expects. For the second round, h is the current g, because the round shifts g into h.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.swapKw: Swaps the two halves of K + W: sha512h wants round t in the upper half and round t+1 in the lower half.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.pairState: Pairs two state words across registers ((d, e) or (f, g)), the operands sha512h reads.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.pairSchedule: Pairs W[t−7] and W[t−6] from two message registers, the operand sha512su1 adds.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.partialFeedFo: Feed-forward, folded: the compiler adds the old (e, f) to the (c, d) of round 77 before T1 of rounds 78 and 79 arrives. That partial sum is not a value of the trace, so the register view keeps showing the old contents; the next add of this register completes H.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.feedForward51: Feed-forward: adds the state from before the block to the state after round 79, giving two words of H.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.copyT1: A copy of the two T1 values: sha512h2 overwrites its destination, but the feed-forward still needs T1 to finish (e, f).
deriver.isa-armv8-sha.note.scheduleAhead: The message schedule runs ahead: this instruction works on W{{first}}, W{{last}} several rounds before the state view's schedule steps write them. The eight message registers hold a sliding window of 16 schedule words.
